SOURCE DIRECTORY

Start at the source.

Use official records or exports from providers you’re authorized to use. Record the source URL and retrieval date; verify the current status before outreach.

Court records

Probate & foreclosure

Find recent case indexes, docket updates, appointed representatives, and recorded filings. Case access varies by user role.

Open Hillsborough HOVER ↗Manual research · Login may be required for probate documents
Parcel records

Ownership & tax mailing

Match exact folio or parcel identifiers. Capture property address, tax mailing address, owner type, building value, and assessed data.

Open Property Appraiser ↗Official parcel lookup & data downloads · Confirm deeds separately
Tax deed research

Tax deed status

Review scheduled sales and current case status. An unpaid certificate, a tax deed application, and a completed sale are different events.

Open tax deed resources ↗Manual research · Check cancellation, redemption, and sale changes
Property condition

Code enforcement

Review open property-maintenance cases and recorded case updates. A complaint is not a verified lien or an owner’s decision to sell.

Open code case search ↗Manual lookup · Verify case status and municipal jurisdiction
Recorded documents

Deeds & recorded liens

Cross-check the latest recorded deed and relevant recorded instruments. Use a title company for closing-level ownership and lien review.

Open recording resources ↗Manual research · Parcel data does not replace a title search

ACQUISITION PLAYBOOK

A repeatable process,
not a bigger unverified list.

Focus on a small, current list you can verify, follow up, and underwrite.

01

Define the buy box

Riverview, Brandon, Temple Terrace, and Tampa. Separate land from houses; retain parcels with no building value. Keep Pasco records in their own county workflow.

02

Combine signals

Review probate plus a matched parcel; then cross-check vacancy, absentee mailing, unpaid taxes, code cases, or foreclosure filings. Merge on parcel ID, never a surname alone.

03

Verify authority

Match case identity to the property owner. Check representative appointment and current property ownership. Identify the estate attorney where relevant.

04

Start a respectful conversation

Use a short introductory letter to a verified mailing address. Build referrals with attorneys, agents, contractors, and title professionals. Let the owner tell you whether selling is useful.

05

Underwrite the opportunity

Confirm condition, asking price, timeline, access, title issues, repair scope, and exit. Use current comparable sales and a written maximum purchase price.

06

Follow up & measure

Track verified records → letters → replies → conversations → offers → contracts. Measure cost per qualified conversation and closed deal by source.

A simple first-contact letter

Hello, my name is Ermias with Baruch-Ermi LLC. I’m a local property investor interested in purchasing properties in your area. If you are considering selling the property at [address], I would be happy to learn about your plans and discuss whether I can help. There is no obligation. If this is not relevant, please disregard this letter.

Add your chosen reply method before mailing. Do not describe an owner as financially distressed or imply knowledge of their personal situation.
